name: tweak
desc: Command-line, ncurses library based hex editor
why: A small ncurses hex editor from Simon Tatham is a compact, well-made door into binary files.

brief.what_it_is: tweak is a command-line hex editor built on the ncurses terminal library. The Homebrew formula describes it as a 'Command-line, ncurses library based hex editor' and installs a single binary named tweak. I could not read the project homepage, so I have no detail on its editing features, file handling, or interface beyond that description. The scout notes attribute it to Simon Tatham, which fits the chiark.greenend.org.uk homepage path, but I did not confirm that from the page.
brief.install_notes: Installs with brew install tweak. The Homebrew formula ships prebuilt bottles for macOS (Apple Silicon and Intel, Big Sur through Golden Gate) and Linux (ARM64 and x86_64), so most users should not need to build from source. The formula uses the macOS system ncurses. No accounts, runtimes, or first-run configuration were mentioned in anything I read.
brief.standout: The scout notes call it a compact, well-made hex editor, but I could not verify that from the homepage or README. From the formula alone, it is a small, single-binary, ncurses-only terminal tool, which is an unusual niche next to larger hex editors.
brief.status: unknown. The Homebrew formula lists stable version 3.02 with bottles for current macOS and Linux releases, which suggests it is still packaged and maintained. The formula page shows 1316 installs over 365 days and zero build errors. I found no commit date or release date, and the upstream homepage was unreachable.
brief.caveats: The upstream homepage was unreachable (URLError), so this brief rests only on the Homebrew formula page and the description supplied with the request. No README or documentation was read, so features, commands, and usage are unknown. Licensing is MIT according to the formula.
